name: Cinderfall Energy
full_legal_name: Cinderfall Energy & Thermal Sovereignty Group, Inc.-S
sovereign_territory: The Cinderfall Thermal Corridor — a network of 11 sovereign subterranean installations drilled beneath the Lake Michigan basin floor and the former industrial zones of Gary, Indiana, collectively spanning an estimated 400 subsurface kilometers
founding_story: Cinderfall was incorporated in 2137 by the Mwangi-Kowalczyk industrial family, who had operated legacy steel mills in the Gary corridor for three generations before the industry collapsed. Rather than abandon their subsurface infrastructure, patriarch Emeka Mwangi-Kowalczyk commissioned a geological survey that revealed unexploited geothermal gradients beneath the old mill sites. The family pivoted entirely, drilling their first thermal tap in 2138 and achieving sovereign corponation status by 2143. The name is both a tribute to the ash-choked skies of their steel mill heritage and a deliberate provocation to environmental regulators.
security_force: The Cinder Watch — 5,500 personnel operating in high-heat environments, trained in subterranean combat and tunnel denial. Cinder Watch soldiers wear ceramic-composite armor rated for environments up to 400°C and are notorious for using thermal lances — repurposed industrial cutting tools — as weapons during territorial disputes. Their subterranean installations are considered among the most defensible sovereign territories in GLMZ.
key_detail: Cinderfall's most significant and least-publicized operation is Project MAGMA TITHE — an ongoing effort to drill to depths that no energy corponation in GLMZ has reached before. Internal leaks suggest they have already achieved a depth of 14 kilometers beneath Lake Michigan, far exceeding any disclosed drilling operation in the corridor. What they have found — or what they are powering with the energy drawn from that depth — is unknown outside the executive tier.
relationship_to_big_20: Member of the Big 20. Holds the energy infrastructure seat and is a direct competitor to Ouroboros Energy, with whom it shares a tense co-existence agreement brokered in 2161 that divides thermal rights above and below 8 kilometers depth. Cinderfall controls the deep; Ouroboros controls the surface-adjacent. Both corponations violate the agreement regularly and deny it publicly.
full_text: Cinderfall Energy & Thermal Sovereignty Group (CDF-S) powers a significant fraction of GLMZ's industrial zones from its network of subterranean geothermal installations beneath the Lake Michigan basin and the Gary industrial corridor. Born from the wreckage of a steel dynasty, the Mwangi-Kowalczyk family transformed generational industrial loss into a Φ1.6 trillion sovereign energy empire. Cinderfall's 88,000 direct employees and 210,000 contracted thermal laborers operate in some of the most physically demanding conditions in the megacity — deep tunnels, high heat, and enforced silence around Project MAGMA TITHE. The Cinder Watch security force, ceramic-armored and thermally equipped, has repelled four attempted hostile annexations since 2155. Within the Big 20, Cinderfall is regarded as blunt, territorial, and profoundly difficult to negotiate with — qualities that Emeka Mwangi-Kowalczyk's descendants consider compliments.
